g.text: ── Ubuntu AI Packaging Mentor — Live Demo ──
— Explains the 'Why' — packaging concepts in plain language.
— Focuses on Ubuntu Policy and compliance.
— Raw output — logs, diffs, system state. No preamble.
✓ Persona set to: Beginner — Explains the 'Why' — packaging concepts in plain language.
Enter path to package source directory:
Enter path to package source directory:
— Legal/copyright analysis — produces a DEP-5 debian/copyright file.
— Dependency discovery — resolves #include headers to Build-Depends packages.
— Changelog generation — summarises git log into debian/changelog format.
— Source patching — manages quilt patch series on upstream source.
The Audit skill scans every source file for its license and copyright holder, then produces a DEP-5 debian/co
pyright file — the machine-readable format Ubuntu's archive requires. Without it your package cannot be uploaded. Think
of it as the legal receipt for all the code you're shipping.
Before saving: verify all copyright holders appear under their Files: stanza, License: identifiers are valid
SPDX names (e.g. GPL-2.0-only), and any third-party vendored code has its own stanza.
[*] LLM budget: 30s (set LLM_BUDGET env var to change)

Review for UNKNOWN license identifiers — those need manual research. Next: run 'lintian' to catch remaining i
ssues, then move on to Detect to fill in your Build-Depends.
Build-Depends lists every package the build system needs before it can compile your source. The Detect skill
scans #include directives and autoconf macros, resolving them to Ubuntu -dev packages automatically — saving you from ch
Before saving: confirm every -dev package exists in the target release ('apt-cache show <pkg>'), remove trans
itively-pulled duplicates, and make sure debhelper-compat is present with the right compat level.
[*] Found: 19 C headers, 0 Python modules, 0 Go modules, 0 build tools
[*] Phase 2: asking AI per dependency (19 items, budget: 30s) ...
Cross-check with 'dpkg-depcheck -d debian/rules build' at build time. Next: run the Scribe skill to draft you
r debian/changelog entry, then test the full build with 'sbuild' or 'pbuilder'.
debian/changelog is the official release history of your package. Each stanza records who changed what and wh
en, and sets the version number dpkg uses. Scribe reads your git history and drafts a properly formatted entry so nothin
g gets lost between commits and release.
Before saving: check the version is higher than the last upload, the suite name matches your target (e.g. 'no
ble'), and the ' -- Name <email> Date' trailer has exactly two spaces between the email and the date.
[*] No git history — drafting Initial release entry
[~] LLM response header did not match — attempting to rescue bullets
[~] No bullets found either — using bare stub
Verify the version bumped correctly and the suite is right. Next: sign with 'debsign' and upload via 'dput' t
o your PPA or the Ubuntu archive.
